title: Reduce trace allocation and unify log-context propagation via lightweight span dispatcher
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Profiling on prod-like load found that span allocation and dynamic context bridging between our tracing SDK and structured logging path account for ~18% of p50 wall-time in hot request paths. This ticket introduces a lightweight span-dispatcher abstraction plus a log-context bridge that: 1) routes spans to exporters without heap-allocating interim objects for the common sync fast-path, 2) exposes a compact inlined trace->log correlation token that logging libraries can read without acquiring locks, and 3) provides a fallback allocation path for edge cases. The goals are to cut span-related allocations by >70% and reduce trace path tail-latency variance. This work focuses on the runtime request path (request handler -> runtime runtime-invocation -> tracing hooks -> exporter), not the backend exporters themselves.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and e2e tests for dispatcher cover sync and async exporters
Benchmark: span allocation per request reduced >= 70% on representative RL workload
No increase in dropped spans or telemetry errors in canary deployment for 72h
Logs contain the new compact trace token and existing log schema remains compatible
implementation_steps: Add lightweight span-dispatcher interface with inline pool and fast-path no-alloc emit
Implement trace-token encoding (12-byte binary -> base64url short token) and provide read API for loggers
Instrument hot paths to use dispatcher instead of current SDK wrapper; keep full-allocation path behind feature flag
Write microbench harness and opentelemetry benchmark script used in prior perf work
Create canary rollout (10% traffic) and monitoring dashboard with error/gap alerts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: token collision or mis-encoding -> Mitigation: include traceID prefix and version byte, add compatibility lookup
Risk: exporters rely on current API shape -> Mitigation: implement adapter for legacy exporters for 1 release cycle
Risk: hidden allocations in logging path -> Mitigation: profile logging hot path and add zero-copy lookup where possible
Risk: increased CPU due to compact encoding -> Mitigation: benchmark CPU tradeoff and gate via rollout if >5% overhead
rollout_plan: Feature branch + unit tests; internal RFC linked below
Benchmarks on perf cluster and compare to baseline (attach results to PR)
Merge behind feature flag; deploy to staging; smoke tests and e2e tracing checks
Canary 10% traffic for 72h with automated alerting; if metrics stable, increase to 50% then full rollout
Deprecate legacy allocation path after two stable releases and update docs
